publishedVisibleTexts: TO CONSIDER 1. To talk about relationships among family members, we normally use the possessive case (‘s) which denotes belonging and possession and in this case states family relationships. 2. There is more than one scenario for the possessive case: a. Joe’s wife is a doctor. - One owner and one possession. b. Those are my aunt’s (kids). - When the noun was already mentioned and we do not need to state again. c. This is Ted and Mary’s child. - Two owners - One possession. d. These are Jake’s and Jill’s children - Two owners and two possessions. 3. When the noun finishes in ‘s’ we only add the (‘) and the end of the word. E.G. This is James’ child. When this happens, we add an extra syllable in spoken language that is pronounced /әz/. 4. This is not only used to talk about family. E.G. Adrian’s car is blue. 5. When we talk about objects or animals, it is common to use: The legs of the table / The tail of the cat. However, you may find examples using the (‘s).

sourceEvidence.publishedTitle: 1 To be + Supposed to In my country, you are supposed to say your first name when introducing yourself. What are you supposed to do when…? To Consider 1. These expressions are not the only ones we can use. 2. There are different ways on how we can ask about customs and traditions. 3. Simple present is also useful to talk about this matter. E:G: We don’t do that here.

sourceEvidence.publishedTitle: 1 Might + Verb simple form David might not answer as usual. The modals are organized from the highest level of probability to the lowest. 2 May + Verb simple form They may attend to the concert, but I would not bet on it. 3 Could + Verb simple form The Jenkins could visit us this weekend; just in case, let’s get some groceries. To Consider 1. All of the three modals deal with probability. 2. Some grammarians establish that might states a higher level of probability. 3. Could can also be used to talk about about abilities, or facts in the past. E.G. She could walk before the accident. 4. Also, could can be used to make formal requests: Could you please call Dan for me?

sourceEvidence.publishedTitle: We can use passive voice for the following functions:
publishedVisibleTexts: We can use passive voice for the following functions:

Functions Examples 1 State what things are made of The legs of the table are iron-made. The spoon was handcrafted in wood. 2 Declare when things are made / done The meeting will be set for tomorrow. Is this piano being played this week? 3 Point who things are made / done by The stuffed clams were made by Jake. Those dresses will be designed by Ericka. 4. Focus on objects rather than subjects in general actions Why was my burger eaten from the fridge? Five points will be taken from your test for cheating.
To consider Passive voice is not only used for the first three aspects; it can also be implemented in regular actions or everyday matters.

publishedVisibleTexts: We are able to express opinions, suggestions and expectations in the past by using the following structures. Check the chart.

STRUCTURES STATEMENTS QUESTIONS Should Have + Past Participle Dylan should have called them before going. What should he have done before going? If it had been me, I should have brought more money. What should you have done? Would have + Past Participle My family would have wanted him to be different, but he wasn’t. How would have your family wanted him to be? He would not have expected me to drop school. Would he have expected you to drop school? Must have + Past Participle We must have seen the straw in the wind, but we did not. Would you have seen the straw in the wind? If he had not done things that way , the boss must have given him the chance. What if he had not done things that way?
